source.document: Lab variant of the MediMeet replication question
source.section: MediMeet Lab: Fresh Reads from Replicas

requirements.text: Keep the provided load balancer, three API servers, one SQL primary and two SQL read replicas.
requirements.reason: Given context: the whole cluster is supplied in the scaffold with scaffold nodes locked against removal; it is not a learner decision, and the sanity checks keep the traffic layer intact.

requirements.text: No read may return data older than the primary has already committed.
Both read replicas must keep serving reads (do not send every read to the primary).
Explain why a read can miss a just-booked appointment even though the write succeeded.
requirements.reason: Observe-and-explain objective: the learner sees follower lag on the canvas and reasons about it in prose; no explanation text is graded.

requirements.text: Explain what stronger read consistency costs (catch-up waits and read latency) and why the lag value itself is not yours to change.
requirements.reason: Observe-and-explain objective: the cost shows in the results (catch-up waits, read latency) but no latency budget is graded, so the lesson is the trade-off, not a number.

requirements.text: Replica lag, write acknowledgement, consensus, election and failover values are question-provided and read-only.
requirements.reason: Given context: these are read-only through constraints.questionOwnedConfigPaths (the consistency model is deliberately left editable as the one configure objective); the grader does not inspect them.
Question-owned scenario input used by the hidden run, not a learner obligation.
Question-owned workload mix used by the hidden run.

advisories.reason: The correctness domain is guided, not exact: only the stale-read oracle is graded, and the oracle is exact within its documented scope (every read on a tracked, replicated datastore is counted).

The read-consistency concept is guided: the grader uses only consistency.staleReads. Session guarantees are not used because Studio scenarios cannot define client sessions, so read-your-writes behaves like eventual here and is deliberately not accepted.
